artists.biography:
Tears for Fears are an English rock band formed in 1981 by Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith.
Founded after the dissolution of their first band, the mod-influenced Graduate, they were initially associated with the New Wave synthesizer bands of the early 1980s but later branched out into mainstream rock and pop, which led to international chart success.
Their platinum-selling debut album, The Hurting, reached number one on the UK Album Chart, while their second album, Songs from the Big Chair, reached number one on the U.S. Billboard 200, achieving multi-platinum status in both the UK and the United States. Following the release of their third platinum-selling album, The Seeds of Love (1989), Smith and Orzabal parted company in 1991, though Orzabal retained the Tears for Fears name throughout the remainder of the 1990s. The duo re-formed in 2000, and released an album of new material, Everybody Loves a Happy Ending, in 2004. To date, Tears for Fears have sold over 25 million albums worldwide, including more than 8 million in the U.S.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1989, The Seeds of Love is the third studio album by English pop rock band Tears For Fears. Departing from the synth-driven sound of their earlier hits, the album embraces a rich, organic blend of rock, pop, and soul, drawing strong influence from 1960s British psychedelia—particularly The Beatles. The record features lush arrangements, prominent use of live instrumentation including horns and piano, and layered production, marking a bold evolution in the band’s musical style. Standout tracks like "Sowing the Seeds of Love" and "Woman in Chains" showcase the group’s songwriting depth and willingness to experiment, while the album’s lyrical themes touch on politics, love, and personal transformation.

The Seeds of Love stands as a pivotal work in Tears For Fears’ discography, following the massive success of Songs From The Big Chair (1985). The four-year gap between albums reflected the band’s desire to craft a more ambitious and artistically mature record, though it also signaled growing creative tensions between Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith. Upon release, the album debuted at number one in the UK and achieved platinum status within weeks, while the single "Sowing the Seeds of Love" reached number two on the US Billboard Hot 100. Though its commercial performance fell slightly short of its predecessor, the album was praised for its sonic ambition and lyrical substance, and has since been recognized as a significant artistic statement in the band’s catalog.
